1	# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site
2	
3	The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
4	features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.
5	
6	## Where things are
7	
8	```
9	astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
10	sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
11	src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
12	src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
13	src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
14	                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
15	src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
16	src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
17	```
18	
19	## The rule that matters
20	
21	**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
22	refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
23	written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
24	probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.
25	
26	Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
27	`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
28	`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
29	`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.
30	
31	## Who reads this
32	
33	Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
34	how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.
35	
36	So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
37	source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
38	of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
39	won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
40	MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.
41	
42	## Voice
43	
44	- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
45	- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
46	- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
47	  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
48	- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
49	  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
50	- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
51	- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
52	  what a reader comes to a reference for.
53	- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.
54	
55	## Page shape
56	
57	```mdx
58	---
59	title: Markers
60	description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
61	---
62	
63	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
64	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
65	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
66	
67	What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.
68	
69	<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />
70	
71	<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />
72	
73	## Add a marker
74	
75	<Steps>
76	
77	1. Move the playhead to the moment.
78	2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.
79	
80	</Steps>
81	
82	## Options
83	
84	| Control | What it does | Default |
85	| ------- | ------------ | ------- |
86	
87	## Good to know
88	
89	Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.
90	
91	## Related
92	
93	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
94	```
95	
96	Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.
97	
98	- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
99	  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
100	- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
101	- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
102	- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
103	- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
104	  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
105	- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
106	  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
107	- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
108	  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
109	  of frame, and give it real alt text.
110	
111	## MDX traps
112	
113	MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
114	code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
115	with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
116	its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.
117	
118	## Checking a page
119	
120	```sh
121	node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
122	python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
123	pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
124	```
125	
126	## Screens
127	
128	The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
129	pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:
130	
131	```sh
132	python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
133	node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
134	```
135	
136	**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
137	path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
138	it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.
139	
140	## When the app changes
141	
142	A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
143	to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
144	menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
145	page that names something internal.
146

1	---
2	title: Markers
3	description: Flag moments on the timeline, name them, jump between them, and turn them into chapters in an exported movie.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A marker is a flag on the ruler that remembers a moment in the project: a beat to cut on, a line to come back to, the start of a chapter.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Mark ▸ Add Marker', 'Mark ▸ Next Marker', 'Mark ▸ Previous Marker']}
12	  keys="M"
13	  where={['The bookmark button in the timeline bar', 'Document tab ▸ Markers']}
14	  tools={['add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Add a marker
18	
19	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same.
20	
21	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Two markers can't share a frame, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one beeps and adds nothing.
22	
23	A marker draws on the ruler as a small flag with a thin line down the ruler, in its colour. An ordinary marker's flag is an outline, and a [chapter](#make-a-chapter) marker's is filled. A project can hold up to 1,024 markers.
24	
25	## Move, rename and remove a marker
26	
27	| To | Do this |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. It snaps, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |
30	| Rename a marker | Double-click its flag, or type in its row in the Document tab. |
31	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
32	
33	Each of these is one undo step.
34	
35	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.
36	
37	## Jump between markers
38	
39	**Mark ▸ Next Marker** and **Mark ▸ Previous Marker** pause playback and move the playhead to the marker. Neither has a keyboard shortcut. They beep when there's no marker further in that direction, and they're dimmed when the project has no markers.
40	
41	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
42	
43	## The Markers list
44	
45	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
46	
47	## Make a chapter
48	
49	Tick **Chapter** in a marker's row. A chapter marker draws as a filled flag, and an ordinary marker as an outline.
50	
51	Chapter markers become chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter takes the marker's name, or "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on when the marker has no name. See [Chapters](/export/chapters/) for how a range export treats them.
52	
53	## Marker colours
54	
55	A marker's colour can only be set by an agent, with `add_marker` or `set_marker`. The colour names are the six [clip label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) colours, and any other name draws the marker in the neutral text colour.
56	
57	## Good to know
58	
59	Markers belong to the whole timeline, not to a nest. While a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open:
60	
61	- The ruler shows no markers, and drags don't snap to them.
62	- The three marker commands in the **Mark** menu are off, and pressing <kbd>M</kbd> beeps.
63	- **Go** is disabled, because the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's own start. Its tooltip says to leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>.
64	- The Document tab's list still shows every marker, and its name field, **Chapter** and **Delete** still work.
65	
66	An agent works to the same rule. With a nest open it can't add a marker or move one, but it can rename one, change its colour or chapter setting, or remove it. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
67	
68	## Related
69	
70	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
71	- [The in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
72	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/)
73

1	---
2	title: Remove Silences
3	description: Find the dead air in a spoken recording, see it on the timeline, and cut it all as one edit.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Remove Silences finds the dead air in a spoken recording, shows you what it would cut, and takes it all out as one undo step, closing the timeline over each cut.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
14	  tools={['detect_silence', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
15	  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Remove the silences
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**. It's available when the timeline has a clip with its sound on. If there turns out to be nothing to measure, Frame Job beeps instead of opening the sheet.
23	
24	2. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet. Both update as you change a control.
25	
26	3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls) until the cuts look right.
27	
28	4. Choose **Remove**.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	<Shot
33	  name="14-remove-silences-sheet.sheet"
34	  alt="The Remove Silences sheet, with Judge by set to Voice, a Level if no voice slider at −40 dBFS, Longer than 0.5 seconds, Keep at ends 0.1 seconds, and In set to All audible clips."
35	/>
36	
37	The sheet opens on its defaults every time. It doesn't remember your last settings.
38	
39	## The controls
40	
41	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
42	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
43	| **Judge by:** | How a moment is tested. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/). | Voice | Voice, Level |
44	| **Quieter than:** or **Level if no voice:** | The level that counts as quiet. The row reads **Quieter than:** in Level mode and **Level if no voice:** in Voice mode. | −40 dBFS | −80 to −10 dBFS |
45	| **Longer than:** | The shortest quiet stretch worth cutting. Shorter pauses, such as the gap between two words, stay. | 0.5 s | 0.05 to 10 s |
46	| **Keep at ends:** | How much of each quiet stretch to keep at each end, so speech doesn't start or stop abruptly. | 0.1 s | 0 to 2 s |
47	| **In:** | Whether to look at **Selected clips** or **All audible clips**. | Selected clips when the selection has something audible, otherwise All audible clips | |
48	
49	**Selected clips** is greyed out when nothing selected makes a sound, and a selection of muted clips counts as nothing audible. Choose it to stop a music bed under a voice-over from holding the cuts up.
50	
51	**Longer than:** measures the stretch as you hear it, before **Keep at ends:** takes its share. A stretch no longer than twice **Keep at ends:** isn't cut. Cuts then snap to the frame grid, so a frame more of room tone can remain. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
52	
53	The two number fields take up to two decimal places. A number outside the range stays in the field and **Remove** beeps until you fix it.
54	
55	## What the sheet tells you
56	
57	The sheet explains itself under the count. It can show more than one of these at once.
58	
59	| The sheet says | What it means |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed." | Nothing in scope makes a sound. With **Selected clips** it reads "Nothing the selected clips play is audible in the mix, so nothing was analysed." |
62	| "The waveform is still being analysed for …" or "Speech is still being analysed for …" | Frame Job hasn't finished with those files, which often happens straight after an import. Leave the sheet open and it updates as each one lands. |
63	| "Quiet inside a nest is left alone…" | A nest held enough quiet to have been cut, so a low count doesn't mean there's no dead air. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and remove its silences there. |
64	
65	Relinking a file starts its analysis again. An open sheet drops the old answers at once and updates when the new ones land.
66	
67	## Good to know
68	
69	- A gap with nothing audible in it is left alone. Remove Silences takes dead air out of a recording, not the gaps you placed between clips. [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) does that.
70	- Nothing inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) is cut, because a nest plays from its first frame and a cut into one would strand the rest of it.
71	- A quiet stretch broken up by a nest or a transition is measured in its pieces.
72	
73	## With an agent
74	
75	`detect_silence` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
76	
77	## Related
78	
79	- [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/)
80	- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
81	- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/)

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. /// that animates: it goes through `binding.ops(video:)` like every number.
extension VideoPane {
    // MARK: Look

    /// Every selected clip that draws has a look (evaluated, as the rows
    /// read); false for no such clip. `ClipPane`'s structure signature reads
    /// it, since it adds or removes the Amount row.
    var allLooked: Bool {
        let clips = binding.videoClips
        return !clips.isEmpty && clips.allSatisfy { binding.video($0).look != nil }
    }

    /// Some selected clip's look is a LUT and its source file is converted
    /// by Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16): a camera LUT applied as a look would
    /// then convert it twice. `ClipPane`'s structure signature reads it, since
    /// it adds or removes the warning row.
    var lutOverCameraLog: Bool {
        let snapshot = binding.snapshot
        return binding.videoClips.contains { clip in
            guard binding.video(clip).look?.kind == .lut,
                let media = clip.source.mediaID, snapshot.media(media)?.color != nil
            else { return false }
            return true
        }

360	/// The Look section's gallery model (spec §11 GR-7 [b], grading GR5b):
361	/// which clips a look applies to, the op a tile or a menu item sends,
362	/// and the nine thumbnails — None and the eight — each the composited frame
363	/// with that tile's click applied, then one per imported `.cube` LUT (spec
364	/// §11 GR-8 [b]), in the media list's order.
365	///
366	/// **It lives on `ClipPane`, not on the view**, because the pane rebuilds its
367	/// sections on every structure change and a thumbnail set that died with each
368	/// build would re-render for nothing. A view attaches itself (`view`) when it
369	/// is built, and an update from any other view — a retired build's late
370	/// `viewDidMoveToWindow` — is ignored.
371	///
372	/// **When it renders.** Its inputs are the edited project's HANDLE, the target
373	/// ids and the thumbnail time. An update or a playhead poke with the inputs it
374	/// last scheduled does nothing; anything else re-arms one `settle` timer, so a
375	/// playhead moving every frame (playback, a scrub) never renders. The timer
376	/// renders only if the gallery is open then (its section expanded, its window
377	/// there); hiding it or leaving the window cancels the timer and supersedes a
378	/// running generation. A generation applies the trial ops (the nine, then one
379	/// per LUT) on main and renders them off main, one tile after another, through
380	/// `Exporter.renderFrame` — `render_frame`'s renderer, so a thumbnail is the
381	/// pixels that tool writes (its file carries PR-11's label; a tile's dump is
382	/// unlabelled, spec §11 PR-11) —
383	/// with `RecipeOptions.none` (thumbnails ignore Show Ungraded, as an export
384	/// does). A superseded generation skips its remaining tiles, and its results
385	/// never land.
386	final class LookGallery {
387	    /// None, then the eight in the core's order: the gallery's reading order.
388	    static let tiles: [LookKind?] = [nil] + LookKind.builtIns.map { Optional($0) }
389	    static let thumbnailWidth = 256
390	    static let settle: TimeInterval = 0.3
391	    #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
392	    /// A launch default naming a folder: each completed generation N writes
393	    /// `<folder>/<N>/<tile>.png` and then `<folder>/<N>/manifest.json`.
394	    static let dumpKey = "RCDevLookGalleryDump"
395	    #endif
396	
397	    private(set) var thumbnails: [CGImage?] = Array(repeating: nil, count: tiles.count)
398	    /// The Imported group's thumbnails, by the LUT's media id.
399	    private(set) var lutThumbnails: [UInt32: CGImage] = [:]
400	    /// The attached view; an update from any other is ignored.
401	    weak var view: LookGalleryView?
402	
403	    private struct Inputs {
404	        let project: ReelProject
405	        let ids: [UInt32]
406	        let time: Ticks
407	
408	        func same(_ other: Inputs?) -> Bool {
409	            guard let other else { return false }
410	            return project === other.project && ids == other.ids && time == other.time
411	        }
412	    }
413	
414	    /// A generation's cancel flag, read off main between tiles.
415	    private final class Token {
416	        private let lock = NSLock()
417	        private var cancelled = false
418	        func cancel() {
419	            lock.lock()
420	            cancelled = true
421	            lock.unlock()
422	        }
423	        var isCancelled: Bool {
424	            lock.lock()
425	            defer { lock.unlock() }
426	            return cancelled
427	        }
428	    }

430	    private weak var document: ProjectDocument?
431	    private var targets: [ClipSnapshot] = []
432	    private var open = false
433	    /// What the last update or poke asked for, what was last scheduled (timer
434	    /// armed, rendering or rendered), and what the thumbnails show.
435	    private var latest: Inputs?
436	    private var scheduled: Inputs?
437	    private var rendered: Inputs?
438	    private var timer: Timer?
439	    private var running: Token?
440	    private var generation = 0

442	    /// The one serial queue the generations render on (a one-frame render

448	    init() {

450	    }

452	    /// Open, and either asked for inputs it has not shown or still rendering.

454	        guard open, let latest else { return false }
455	        return !latest.same(rendered) || running != nil

458	    // MARK: - Updates
459	
460	    func update(
461	        from view: LookGalleryView, document: ProjectDocument?, targets: [ClipSnapshot],
462	        open: Bool
463	    ) {
464	        guard view === self.view else { return }
465	        self.document = document
466	        self.targets = targets
467	        self.open = open
468	        reschedule()
469	    }
470	
471	    /// The playhead moved in `document`: each of its live galleries asks again.
472	    static func playheadMoved(in document: ProjectDocument) {
473	        for gallery in live.allObjects where gallery.document === document {
474	            gallery.reschedule()
475	        }
476	    }
477	
478	    private func reschedule() {
479	        guard open, let document, let first = targets.first else {
480	            latest = nil
481	            cancel()
482	            return
483	        }
484	        let inputs = Inputs(
485	            project: document.editedProject, ids: targets.map(\.id),
486	            time: Self.time(first: first, playhead: document.playhead))
487	        latest = inputs
488	        if inputs.same(scheduled) { return }
489	        cancel()
490	        scheduled = inputs
491	        if inputs.same(rendered) { return }
492	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: Self.settle, repeats: false) { [weak self] _ in
493	            self?.fire()
494	        }
495	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
496	        self.timer = timer
497	    }

499	    /// Stops the timer and supersedes a running generation; what was last
500	    /// scheduled falls back to what the thumbnails show.
501	    private func cancel() {
502	        timer?.invalidate()
503	        timer = nil
504	        running?.cancel()
505	        running = nil
506	        scheduled = rendered
507	    }

509	    // MARK: - A generation
510	
511	    private func fire() {
512	        timer = nil
513	        guard open, let view, view.window != nil, let document, let inputs = scheduled,
514	              !inputs.same(rendered)
515	        else {
516	            // Nothing rendered, so a later update with these inputs must arm again.
517	            scheduled = rendered
518	            return
519	        }
520	        generation += 1
521	        let number = generation
522	        let token = Token()
523	        running = token
524	        func trial(_ edit: ReelEdit?) -> ReelProject? {
525	            switch edit {
526	            case .applied(let project)?: return project
527	            case .identity?: return inputs.project
528	            default: return nil
529	            }
530	        }
531	        let luts = Self.luts(in: inputs.project.snapshot).map(\.id)
532	        let trials: [ReelProject?] = Self.tiles.map { tile in
533	            trial(try? inputs.project.applying(Self.op(tile, clips: inputs.ids)))
534	        } + luts.map { lut in
535	            trial(try? inputs.project.applying(Self.op(lut: lut, clips: inputs.ids)))
536	        }
537	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
538	        let graphics = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
539	        var dump: URL?
540	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
541	        if let folder = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: Self.dumpKey), !folder.isEmpty {
542	            dump = URL(fileURLWithPath: folder).appendingPathComponent(String(number))
543	        }
544	        #endif
545	        Self.queue.async { [weak self] in
546	            var images: [CGImage?] = []
547	            for trial in trials {
548	                if token.isCancelled { return }
549	                images.append(trial.flatMap {
550	                    Exporter.renderFrame(
551	                        project: $0, urls: urls, at: inputs.time, maxWidth: Self.thumbnailWidth,
552	                        options: .none, graphics: graphics)
553	                })
554	            }
555	            if token.isCancelled { return }
556	            let names = Self.tiles.map { $0?.rawValue ?? "none" } + luts.map { "lut-\($0)" }
557	            if let dump { Self.write(images, names, generation: number, inputs: inputs, to: dump) }
558	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
559	                guard let self, self.running === token, !token.isCancelled else { return }
560	                self.running = nil
561	                self.thumbnails = Array(images.prefix(Self.tiles.count))
562	                self.lutThumbnails = [:]
563	                for (lut, image) in zip(luts, images.dropFirst(Self.tiles.count)) {
564	                    self.lutThumbnails[lut] = image
565	                }
566	                self.rendered = inputs
567	                self.view?.showThumbnails()
568	            }
569	        }
570	    }

572	    /// The dev dump: the PNGs (the nine, then `lut-<id>`), then the
573	    /// manifest, last, with `tiles` the names in order.
574	    private static func write(
575	        _ images: [CGImage?], _ names: [String], generation: Int, inputs: Inputs, to folder: URL
576	    ) {
577	        try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
578	        var missing: [String] = []
579	        for (name, image) in zip(names, images) {
580	            guard let image else {
581	                missing.append(name)
582	                continue
583	            }
584	            _ = try? FrameWriter.write(
585	                image, as: .png, to: folder.appendingPathComponent(name + ".png"))
586	        }
587	        let manifest: [String: Any] = [
588	            "generation": generation, "t": inputs.time, "clips": inputs.ids, "missing": missing,
589	            "tiles": names,
590	        ]

1016	/// Imported LUTs' lattices (spec §11 GR-8): a LUT look's `.cube` file read
1017	/// through `MediaImporter.readLUT` and uploaded as an `rgba16Float` `size³`
1018	/// 3D texture, alpha 1 and every value clamped to 0–1, which step 4d samples
1019	/// at `texture(2)` exactly as it samples a built-in look's bake.
1020	///
1021	/// Kept in a least-recently-used cache of `capacity`, keyed by the file's
1022	/// path, byte size and modification date — so a LUT changed on disk is read
1023	/// again at the next frame drawn — with a file that cannot be read or
1024	/// uploaded cached as a failure under its key, so a refused or broken file
1025	/// is not re-read every frame (a missing file has no key and answers nil at
1026	/// once). The attributes are read through `FileManager` each time, never
1027	/// through `URL.resourceValues`, which caches them on the URL. One lock, as
1028	/// `LookTextures`' cache has: the preview's and an export's compositors
1029	/// render on their own queues.
1030	final class LutTextures {
1031	    static let capacity = 8
1032	
1033	    private struct Key: Hashable {
1034	        let path: String
1035	        let size: Int
1036	        let modified: Date
1037	    }
1038	
1039	    private enum Entry {
1040	        case texture(MTLTexture)
1041	        case failed
1042	    }
1043	
1044	    private let device: MTLDevice
1045	    private let lock = NSLock()
1046	    private var cache = LRUCache<Key, Entry>(limit: LutTextures.capacity)
1047	
1048	    init(device: MTLDevice) {
1049	        self.device = device
1050	    }
1051	
1052	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
1053	        fatalError("LutTextures does not support NSCoder")
1054	    }

1056	    /// The lattice of the `.cube` file at `url`, read and uploaded on a miss;
1057	    /// nil when the file is missing, refused by the core or cannot be
1058	    /// uploaded.
1059	    func texture(at url: URL) -> MTLTexture? {
1060	        let path = url.standardizedFileURL.path
1061	        guard let attributes = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: path),
1062	            let bytes = (attributes[.size] as? NSNumber)?.intValue,
1063	            let modified = attributes[.modificationDate] as? Date
1064	        else { return nil }
1065	        let key = Key(path: path, size: bytes, modified: modified)
1066	        lock.lock()
1067	        defer { lock.unlock() }
1068	        if let hit = cache.value(for: key) {
1069	            if case .texture(let texture) = hit { return texture }
1070	            return nil
1071	        }
1072	        let made = (try? MediaImporter.readLUT(url)).flatMap { upload($0) }
1073	        cache.insert(made.map { .texture($0) } ?? .failed, for: key)
1074	        return made
1075	    }

1077	    /// The table as `rgba16Float` texels, each value clamped to 0–1 and
1078	    /// alpha 1, converted to half floats by vImage (round to nearest).
1079	    private func upload(_ lattice: CubeLattice) -> MTLTexture? {
1080	        let n = lattice.size
1081	        let points = n * n * n
1082	        guard n >= 2, lattice.rgb.count == points * 3 else { return nil }
1083	        var rgba = [Float](repeating: 1, count: points * 4)
1084	        for point in 0..<points {
1085	            for channel in 0..<3 {
1086	                rgba[point * 4 + channel] = min(max(lattice.rgb[point * 3 + channel], 0), 1)
1087	            }
1088	        }
1089	        let count = rgba.count
1090	        var halves = [UInt16](repeating: 0, count: count)
1091	        let converted: Bool = rgba.withUnsafeMutableBytes { source in
1092	            halves.withUnsafeMutableBytes { target in
1093	                guard let from = source.baseAddress, let to = target.baseAddress else {
1094	                    return false
1095	                }
1096	                var src = vImage_Buffer(
1097	                    data: from, height: 1, width: vImagePixelCount(count),
1098	                    rowBytes: source.count)
1099	                var dst = vImage_Buffer(
1100	                    data: to, height: 1, width: vImagePixelCount(count),
1101	                    rowBytes: target.count)
1102	                return vImageConvert_PlanarFtoPlanar16F(&src, &dst, vImage_Flags(kvImageNoFlags))
1103	                    == kvImageNoError
1104	            }
1105	        }

## Looks and LUTs

### Built-in looks

**Look** is a gallery of tiles. Each tile is a thumbnail of the first selected clip with that look applied: the frame at the playhead when the playhead is inside that clip, otherwise the clip's first frame. The thumbnails refresh a moment after the playhead stops or an edit lands, never during playback or scrubbing, and only while the Look section is open. **None** comes first, then the eight looks:

| Look | Character |
|---|---|
| Warm | Warmer white balance, golden highlights |
| Cool | Cooler white balance, blue shadows |
| Teal & Orange | Teal shadows, orange highlights, more contrast |
| Vivid | More contrast and vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites |
| Faded | Low contrast, muted colour, lifted blacks |
| Vintage | Muted and warm, with a fade and split-toned shadows and highlights |
| Dramatic | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows |
| Black & White | Monochrome |

Click a tile to put that look on every selected clip. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined. If a clip already had a look, it keeps its amount; a clip with no look gets 100 %. **None** (or the section's **Reset**) removes the look. The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even while Show Ungraded is on.

**Amount** (0–100 %, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % behind the field's chevron) sets how much of the look applies. The row only appears when every selected clip has a look.

**Clip ▸ Look ▸** does the same from the menu: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**. A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some carry. The menu items have no shortcut, and the menu is unavailable when no selected clip can take a grade.

### Imported .cube LUTs

A `.cube` 3D LUT is media in your project. You can add one three ways:

- **Import LUT…**, the button under the gallery, picks a `.cube` file and applies it to the selected clips, all in one undo step ("Import LUT").
- **File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I) adds it to the project.
- Dropping the file on the Media tab also adds it.

Each LUT gets a tile in the gallery's **Imported** group, named after its file without `.cube`. It also gets an item in **Clip ▸ Look ▸** between the eight looks and None. A LUT is applied at the same step as a built-in look and uses the same **Amount** row.

Frame Job reads 3D LUTs whose `LUT_3D_SIZE` is from 2 to 65. It refuses any other file in its own words, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." Output values are clamped to 0–1. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read at the next frame drawn. If the file goes missing, the clip draws without its look until you relink it; the rest of the grade still applies.

The Look section warns you in two cases:

- "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." A creative LUT is fine there; a camera LUT would convert the footage a second time.
- "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709."

See [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) for camera log and HLG projects.

**Removing a LUT.** A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, and by every file whose Camera Log it is. Removing it from the Media tab asks first, naming those uses, and its **Remove and Clear Looks** button removes the LUT and clears the look from those clips (they keep their place) and the Camera Log from those files. An action whose end names the removed LUT simply stops changing the look.

*Agents:* `set_video` with `look: {kind, amount}`. `kind` is one of `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white` or `lut`, and `look: null` removes the look. For a LUT, call `import_media` with the `.cube` file, then `set_video {look: {kind: "lut", media: <id>}}`.

478	    private func reschedule() {
479	        guard open, let document, let first = targets.first else {
480	            latest = nil
481	            cancel()

484	        let inputs = Inputs(
485	            project: document.editedProject, ids: targets.map(\.id),

511	    private func fire() {
512	        timer = nil
513	        guard open, let view, view.window != nil, let document, let inputs = scheduled,
514	              !inputs.same(rendered)
515	        else {
516	            // Nothing rendered, so a later update with these inputs must arm again.
517	            scheduled = rendered
518	            return
519	        }
520	        generation += 1
521	        let number = generation
522	        let token = Token()
523	        running = token
524	        func trial(_ edit: ReelEdit?) -> ReelProject? {
525	            switch edit {
526	            case .applied(let project)?: return project
527	            case .identity?: return inputs.project
528	            default: return nil
529	            }
530	        }
531	        let luts = Self.luts(in: inputs.project.snapshot).map(\.id)
532	        let trials: [ReelProject?] = Self.tiles.map { tile in
533	            trial(try? inputs.project.applying(Self.op(tile, clips: inputs.ids)))
534	        } + luts.map { lut in
535	            trial(try? inputs.project.applying(Self.op(lut: lut, clips: inputs.ids)))
536	        }
537	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
538	        let graphics = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
539	        var dump: URL?
540	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
541	        if let folder = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: Self.dumpKey), !folder.isEmpty {
542	            dump = URL(fileURLWithPath: folder).appendingPathComponent(String(number))
543	        }
544	        #endif
545	        Self.queue.async { [weak self] in
546	            var images: [CGImage?] = []
547	            for trial in trials {
548	                if token.isCancelled { return }
549	                images.append(trial.flatMap {
550	                    Exporter.renderFrame(
551	                        project: $0, urls: urls, at: inputs.time, maxWidth: Self.thumbnailWidth,
552	                        options: .none, graphics: graphics)
553	                })
554	            }
555	            if token.isCancelled { return }
556	            let names = Self.tiles.map { $0?.rawValue ?? "none" } + luts.map { "lut-\($0)" }
557	            if let dump { Self.write(images, names, generation: number, inputs: inputs, to: dump) }
558	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
559	                guard let self, self.running === token, !token.isCancelled else { return }
560	                self.running = nil
561	                self.thumbnails = Array(images.prefix(Self.tiles.count))
562	                self.lutThumbnails = [:]
563	                for (lut, image) in zip(luts, images.dropFirst(Self.tiles.count)) {
564	                    self.lutThumbnails[lut] = image
565	                }
566	                self.rendered = inputs
567	                self.view?.showThumbnails()
568	            }
569	        }
570	    }

572	    /// The dev dump: the PNGs (the nine, then `lut-<id>`), then the
573	    /// manifest, last, with `tiles` the names in order.
574	    private static func write(
575	        _ images: [CGImage?], _ names: [String], generation: Int, inputs: Inputs, to folder: URL
576	    ) {
577	        try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
578	        var missing: [String] = []
579	        for (name, image) in zip(names, images) {
580	            guard let image else {
581	                missing.append(name)
582	                continue
583	            }
584	            _ = try? FrameWriter.write(
585	                image, as: .png, to: folder.appendingPathComponent(name + ".png"))
586	        }
587	        let manifest: [String: Any] = [
588	            "generation": generation, "t": inputs.time, "clips": inputs.ids, "missing": missing,
589	            "tiles": names,
590	        ]
591	        if let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: manifest) {
592	            try? data.write(to: folder.appendingPathComponent("manifest.json"))
593	        }
594	    }

## Looks and LUTs

### Built-in looks

**Look** is a gallery of tiles. Each tile is a thumbnail of the first selected clip with that look applied: the frame at the playhead when the playhead is inside that clip, otherwise the clip's first frame. The thumbnails refresh a moment after the playhead stops or an edit lands, never during playback or scrubbing, and only while the Look section is open. **None** comes first, then the eight looks:

| Look | Character |
|---|---|
| Warm | Warmer white balance, golden highlights |
| Cool | Cooler white balance, blue shadows |
| Teal & Orange | Teal shadows, orange highlights, more contrast |
| Vivid | More contrast and vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites |
| Faded | Low contrast, muted colour, lifted blacks |
| Vintage | Muted and warm, with a fade and split-toned shadows and highlights |
| Dramatic | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows |
| Black & White | Monochrome |

Click a tile to put that look on every selected clip. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined. If a clip already had a look, it keeps its amount; a clip with no look gets 100 %. **None** (or the section's **Reset**) removes the look. The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even while Show Ungraded is on.

**Amount** (0–100 %, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % behind the field's chevron) sets how much of the look applies. The row only appears when every selected clip has a look.

**Clip ▸ Look ▸** does the same from the menu: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**. A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some carry. The menu items have no shortcut, and the menu is unavailable when no selected clip can take a grade.

### Imported .cube LUTs

A `.cube` 3D LUT is media in your project. You can add one three ways:

- **Import LUT…**, the button under the gallery, picks a `.cube` file and applies it to the selected clips, all in one undo step ("Import LUT").
- **File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I) adds it to the project.
- Dropping the file on the Media tab also adds it.

Each LUT gets a tile in the gallery's **Imported** group, named after its file without `.cube`. It also gets an item in **Clip ▸ Look ▸** between the eight looks and None. A LUT is applied at the same step as a built-in look and uses the same **Amount** row.

Frame Job reads 3D LUTs whose `LUT_3D_SIZE` is from 2 to 65. It refuses any other file in its own words, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." Output values are clamped to 0–1. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read at the next frame drawn. If the file goes missing, the clip draws without its look until you relink it; the rest of the grade still applies.

The Look section warns you in two cases:

- "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." A creative LUT is fine there; a camera LUT would convert the footage a second time.
- "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709."

See [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) for camera log and HLG projects.

**Removing a LUT.** A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, and by every file whose Camera Log it is. Removing it from the Media tab asks first, naming those uses, and its **Remove and Clear Looks** button removes the LUT and clears the look from those clips (they keep their place) and the Camera Log from those files. An action whose end names the removed LUT simply stops changing the look.

*Agents:* `set_video` with `look: {kind, amount}`. `kind` is one of `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white` or `lut`, and `look: null` removes the look. For a LUT, call `import_media` with the `.cube` file, then `set_video {look: {kind: "lut", media: <id>}}`.

## Grading inside an action

Every grade setting can be animated. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from the clip's own value. The row marks (◆) and the Color tab's badge show which settings the selected action animates. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) for actions.

- **Light, Color, wheels, Strength, the look's Amount and the qualifier's numbers** ramp smoothly. An animated hue centre takes the short way round the colour wheel; 350° to 10° passes through 0°.
- **Curves** animate between any two curves, even with different numbers of points, and from or to a straight line. Inside an action, a channel cell's **Reset Red** (or whichever channel) and the row's **Set end value to default** write a straight curve to the action's end, so the curve animates back to neutral.
- **Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself, not to the action**, even with an action selected. A look that differs between start and end switches at the action's end. Amount is what animates.
- **Turning a qualifier range on or off** switches at the action's end.

While an action is selected, a grade section's header shows **Clear** in place of **Reset**, and only when the action animates one of that section's rows: it removes the section's settings from the action. Right-click a grade row for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**.

The grade controls show the action's animation in their own way:

- **Wheel disc:** a hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead.
- **Wheel strip:** filled in action colour from the start value, with a coral tick at the playhead's value.
- **Curve plot:** the action's start curve dashed, and the edited curve and its points in action colour.
- **Qualifier strip:** the band outlined and its knobs drawn in action colour.

Sliders carry the same marks as everywhere else in the inspector; see [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

*Agents:* `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with a `video` patch carrying `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look.amount` or `qualifier`.

## Copying a grade: Paste Attributes

Copy a graded clip (⌘C), select other clips, and choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V). The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's in one undo step: its grade, look, filters and the rest of its picture settings, including position and scale. Where the copied clip has sound, its audio settings come too. A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label are never copied.

Qualifiers follow the clip type:

- Pasting onto an ordinary clip drops the qualifier.
- Pasting from an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip keeps the adjustment clip's own qualifier.
- Between two adjustment clips, the qualifier is copied.

Pasting a clip that has blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode onto an adjustment clip is refused.

*Agents:* `paste_attributes`, which takes `groups` (`video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`) to copy only some of them.

## Limits

- The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable. Deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
- Qualifiers exist only on adjustment clips. To grade one colour, put an adjustment clip above the picture for the span you want. It grades every track behind it, so a matte track cutting its track is how you confine it to one area (see [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)).
- There is no Offset wheel. Use Color's **Brightness** for an overall lift.
- Show Ungraded, Show Selection and the scopes affect only the window's preview. Nothing about them is saved or exported.
- A curve holds at most 16 points and at least 2.
- Only 3D `.cube` LUTs with a size of 2 to 65 are read.

See also: [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md) for blend modes, filters and mattes, [Export](export.md) for writing the graded film, and [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) for every key.

5:Grading itself (Light, Color, curves, looks and the scopes) is covered in [Colour grading](color-grading.md). The export sheet as a whole is covered in [Export](export.md).
13:| Ordinary Rec. 709 or untagged video, stills, recordings | Drawn as is | Lifted to HDR reference white (203 cd/m², HLG 75 %), so it looks the same as it does in SDR |
17:| Camera log (set in the Media tab) | Converted to a normal-looking Rec. 709 picture | Converted to real HDR |
26:Log footage looks flat and grey until it is converted. The **Camera Log** section of the **Media** tab tells Frame Job which curve a video file was shot with. The section appears once the project has a video file.
31:It is a setting on the *file*, so every clip of that file follows it, reversed clips included. It is one undo step, **Camera Log**. A line under the popup says what is set. It reads "Select a video in the list" when the selected row is not a video file, and the popup is disabled. The section's header shows the selected file's setting (its curve or LUT name), so you can read it with the section collapsed.
49:| LUT: *name* | Each `.cube` LUT already in the project | — |
50:| Use LUT… | Choose a `.cube` file that converts this file's log to Rec. 709 | — |
58:An iPhone **Apple Log** or **Apple Log 2** file is recognised by its label when you import it, so it looks like normal video straight away. The line under the popup then adds "— from the file", for example "Apple Log — from the file". Sony, Panasonic and Canon files carry no label Frame Job can read, so choose their curve by hand. To see an Apple Log file's raw log picture, choose **None**.
60:### Using your own LUT
62:**Use LUT…** opens a file panel asking you to "Choose a .cube LUT that converts this file's log footage to Rec. 709." The LUT is added to the project's media list and becomes this file's conversion, all in one **Camera Log** step. Its output is taken as Rec. 709. Other files can then pick it from the popup as **LUT: *name***. If that LUT is already in the Media list, its entry is reused instead of a second one being added. A file that can't be read as a LUT shows an error.
64:A LUT that is some file's Camera Log counts as used: **Unused only** hides it, and Remove asks first.
66:If you remove that LUT from the Media list, the alert says how many files use it as their Camera Log, for example "the Camera Log of 2 files, which lose it". **Remove and Clear Looks** removes it, and those files go back to no conversion.
68:### Camera Log and looks
70:Camera Log is applied before any look. If a clip's file is converted by Camera Log and you also give the clip a camera LUT as a look, the Look section warns: "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." It is only a warning, because a creative LUT on top is legitimate. See [Colour grading](color-grading.md).
72:*Agents:* `set_media_color` (`color` is `{log, gamut?}`, `{lut}` or `null`); `get_project`'s `media[].color` shows `detected: true` for a file set at import.
76:A PQ (HDR10) file has its highlights roll off to white at the brightness its own metadata names. Import reads the peak from the file: MaxCLL first, then the mastering display's maximum. It looks in the file's sample description and, when that names none, in the video stream's own HDR10 metadata (HEVC SEI, or AV1 metadata), so files from ffmpeg, HandBrake or x265 are read too. A file that names no peak is treated as 1,000 cd/m².
110:- **SDR material is lifted to HDR reference white.** That covers SDR video, stills, screen recordings, titles, captions, shapes, graphics, the background and shadow colours. White is fixed at 203 cd/m² (HLG 75 %), so SDR material looks as it did and HDR highlights rise above it. There is no setting for the reference white.
115:- **A `.cube` look reads its values as Rec. 709.** The Look section warns: "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709."
154:The change is one undo step, **Blending**. It changes no clip and no grade. Grades, the chroma key, qualifiers, Show Selection, luma mattes and the scopes still read the same values they did, so a grade looks the same either way. In an HDR (HLG) project, "linear" means HLG's scene light.
192:- **Camera Log needs a video file.** It is refused on an audio file, an image or a LUT. A PQ still takes only a peak.

---
title: "Looks"
description: "Put one of eight built-in colour treatments on a clip by its picture, set how much of it applies, and take it off again."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A look is a finished colour treatment you put on a clip in one click and then dial back to taste. It sits on top of your own grade, so it doesn't move the Light, Color, Wheels or Curves controls, and taking it off leaves them as they were.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Look"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

## Apply a look

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts collapsed.

3. Click a tile.

4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
/>

The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.

## The Look gallery

The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.

Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

## The eight looks

Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls, plus a tint pushed into the shadows, the highlights or both.

| Look | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |

## Live thumbnails

Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.

The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.

The tiles refresh about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. They never refresh during playback or a scrub, and they only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.

The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.

## Amount

**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.

The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.

Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Remove a look

Do any one of these:

- Click the **None** tile.
- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.

The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.

## Apply a look from the menu

**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.

A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.

The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone.

## The Look summary

The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section collapsed.

| The header reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |

## Looks on stills and adjustment clips

A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. Text, shapes, graphics and nests don't take one.

On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.

## Good to know

- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings.

## With an agent

An agent sets a look and its amount in one step with `set_video`, and removes it the same way. It can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. The amount animates, and a change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

---
title: ".cube LUTs"
description: "Bring a .cube colour table into a project, use it as a clip's look, and know what happens when the file changes, goes missing or is removed."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A `.cube` LUT is a colour table from a grading tool, a camera maker or a LUT pack. In Frame Job it's a file in your project, like footage. You add it once, then use it as a clip's [look](/color/looks/), or as the conversion for a [log file](/hdr/log-luts/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Look', 'File ▸ Add Media…']}
  keys="⇧⌘I"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…', 'Media tab']}
  tools={['import_media', 'set_video', 'remove_media']}
/>

## Import and apply a LUT

<Steps>

1. Select the clips you want to grade.

2. Open the **Look** section of the **Color** sub-tab, and click **Import LUT…** under the gallery. The button is off when no selected clip can take a grade.

3. Choose a `.cube` file.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="05e-clip-look-lut.inspector"
  alt="The Look section with the eight built-in look tiles and None, then an Imported group holding two tiles, Warm Print and Bleach, with Warm Print outlined in blue. The Import LUT… button sits underneath, and the section header reads Warm Print 80%."
/>

The file joins the project and goes on the selected clips as one undo step, **Import LUT**. If the file is already in the project, Frame Job reuses its entry rather than adding it twice. If Frame Job can't read the file, an error appears and nothing changes.

## Add a LUT without applying it

Add the file to the project and apply it later:

- Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>). A file with the `.cube` extension, in any case, counts as a LUT.
- Or drop the file on the **Media** tab. The tab is the only place that takes a dropped `.cube`.

## Apply a LUT already in the project

Every LUT in the project is offered in two places, in the order of the Media list:

- **The gallery.** Its tile sits in the **Imported** group, in rows of three, and previews the LUT on your frame like any [live thumbnail](/color/looks/#live-thumbnails). The tile's name is the file's name without `.cube`. With no LUTs in the project, the group isn't there.
- **The menu.** It's an item in **Clip ▸ Look**, between the eight looks and **None**.

Both work as they do for a built-in look, on every selected clip, as one undo step, **Look**.

## A LUT is a look

A LUT applied to a clip behaves like a built-in look. It comes at the same point in the grade, uses the same [**Amount**](/color/looks/#amount) row, and is removed the same way. A clip that had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with none gets 100%. A clip holds one look, so a LUT replaces a built-in look, and a built-in look replaces a LUT.

## LUT rows on the Media tab

A LUT appears in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with a cube icon, and its tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."

A LUT never goes on the timeline. You can't drag its row, **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are off in its right-click menu, and the same commands in the menu bar stay dimmed while its row is selected.

The rest of the row works as it does for footage:

- **Reveal in Timeline** selects the clips whose look it is.
- **Reveal in Finder** and **Relink…** find the file. A LUT relinks only to another `.cube` file.
- **Unused only** hides a LUT only when no clip and no file's Camera Log uses it.
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the file into the project with everything else.

## Supported .cube files

Frame Job reads 3D LUTs in a text `.cube` file of up to 32 MB.

| In the file | What Frame Job does |
| --- | --- |
| `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65 | Reads it. The line is required, and it comes before the table. |
| `TITLE`, `#` comments, blank lines | Reads past them. |
| Windows line endings or a UTF-8 byte order mark | Reads them. |
| `DOMAIN_MIN 0 0 0`, `DOMAIN_MAX 1 1 1`, `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0 1` | Accepts them, because they're the defaults. |
| Table values outside 0 to 1 | Accepts them, and clamps them to 0 to 1 when drawing. |

Anything else is turned down, with the line it stopped at:

- A 1D LUT.
- A `LUT_3D_SIZE` outside 2 to 65, or a second `LUT_3D_SIZE` line.
- A domain or input range that isn't the default.
- A keyword Frame Job doesn't know, or any keyword after the table.
- A table with too few or too many rows, or a row without three numbers.
- A value that isn't a finite number.

The message reads, for example, "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."

The section warns you in two cases. Neither stops you, and the LUT still applies.

| The warning | When it shows | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and its file has a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) setting. | A creative LUT is fine there. A camera LUT would convert the footage a second time. |
| "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and the [project is HDR](/hdr/dynamic-range/). | The LUT keeps its 0-to-1 meaning, so one made for Rec. 709 may not suit the HLG picture. |

## A changed file

Frame Job refers to the `.cube` file rather than copying it. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read the next time a frame is drawn. There's nothing to import again.

## A missing or broken file

If the file goes missing, or can't be read any more, the clip draws without its look. The rest of its grade still applies, and the look stays on the clip. A clip's look comes back once the file is back.

A missing LUT shows the **missing** badge in the Media tab, and it's in the list Frame Job offers to [relink](/projects/relink-media/) when the project opens. A file that's there but broken has no badge: the look just doesn't draw until you fix the file or relink it.

## Remove a LUT in use

A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, on the timeline or in a nest, and by every file whose Camera Log it is.

<Steps>

1. In the Media tab, right-click the LUT's row and choose **Remove**.

2. Read the alert, which counts the uses. For example, "It is the look of 3 clips, which keep their place and lose the look."

3. Choose **Remove and Clear Looks**, or **Cancel**.

</Steps>

**Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT, clears the look from those clips and clears the Camera Log from those files, as one undo step, **Remove Media**. The clips stay where they are. An unused LUT is removed straight away, with no alert.

## With an agent

An agent adds the file with `import_media`, then applies it with `set_video`, naming the LUT's media id. It can't place a LUT as a clip: `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` and `add_background` turn it down and say how to apply it instead. `remove_media` won't remove a LUT in use unless it's asked to clear those uses, which is what **Remove and Clear Looks** does.

An agent can also name a LUT at an action's end. That action stays if the LUT is removed, and draws no look at its end. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [Looks](/color/looks/)

- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/)
- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)

---
title: "Looks"
description: "Put one of eight built-in colour treatments on a clip by its picture, set how much of it applies, and take it off again."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A look is a finished colour treatment you put on a clip in one click and then dial back to taste. It sits on top of your own grade, so it doesn't move the Light, Color, Wheels or Curves controls, and taking it off leaves them as they were.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Look"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

## Apply a look

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts collapsed.

3. Click a tile.

4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
/>

The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.

## The Look gallery

The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.

Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

## The eight looks

Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls, plus a tint pushed into the shadows, the highlights or both.

| Look | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |

## Live thumbnails

Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.

The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.

The tiles refresh about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. They never refresh during playback or a scrub, and they only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.

The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.

## Amount

**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.

The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.

Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Remove a look

Do any one of these:

- Click the **None** tile.
- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.

The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.

## Apply a look from the menu

**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.

A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.

The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone.

## The Look summary

The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section collapsed.

| The header reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |

## Looks on stills and adjustment clips

A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. Text, shapes, graphics and nests don't take one.

On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.

## Good to know

- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings.

## With an agent

An agent sets a look and its amount in one step with `set_video`, and removes it the same way. It can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. The amount animates, and a change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

It can't place a LUT as a clip: `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` and `add_background` turn it down and say how to apply it instead. `remove_media` won't remove a LUT in use unless it's asked to clear those uses, which is what **Remove and Clear Looks** does.

An agent can also name a LUT at an action's end. That action stays if the LUT is removed, and draws no look at its end. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
